svg.title: The CIA Triad and GKOS v0.81
svg.desc: Three rows map the FIPS 199 security objectives to GKOS v0.81. Confidentiality: authorization precedes protected disclosure on every surface (GKOS-DISCLOSURE-001), sensitivity fails closed, authority and effect scope carry audience and sensitivity limits, and Context Manifests are restriction-aware; the implementation adds enforcement, encryption, key management and leak tests. Integrity, the strongest alignment: state-change receipts, deterministic canonical hashing, stable identity and lineage, append-only decisions with distinct actor roles, and exact manifest and authority binding at action time; the implementation adds tamper-resistant storage, signing, trusted time and tests. Availability, partial: recorded refusal distinct from outage, recovery routes on every authorized use, hold-aware retention, and queue governance; the implementation adds backups, redundancy, service objectives and incident response. A strip shows where each objective concentrates across layers L1 to L7. Informative; not a conformance or security claim.
svg.text: The CIA Triad and GKOS v0.81
How the governed evidence GKOS requires supports confidentiality, integrity and availability — and what a deployment still has to add
Informative · not a conformance or security claim
Authorization before any protected disclosure — including logs, metrics,
errors and diagnostics; denied data must not influence outputs
Missing sensitivity fails closed; restrictions raise at once, lower only
with authenticated authority; audit inherits sensitivity
Authority scoped by purpose, tenant, audience and sensitivity;
delegation can only narrow; effect scope has a sensitivity ceiling
Context Manifests bind purpose, recipient and restrictions;
Viewers show restrictions without gaining authority
Where: L1 sensitivity evidence · L4 control and Refusal Receipts · L6 Selection Envelope and Context Manifest · L7 Authority Receipt and Authorized Use Record
Enforcement at the real operation, not
Encryption at rest and in transit; key,
Leak tests across every surface: logs, errors,
Every committed state change is bound to a State-Change Receipt or it
fails closed / rolls back / compensates before commit success
Deterministic GKX-CBOR-1 encoding and SHA-256 hashing; stable identity;
lineage keeps every branch, no tiebreak picks a winner
Append-only Decision Records; distinct proposer / reviewer / authorizer /
executor; no self-approval; bounded different-model agent review
Manifest hash equal at authorization and action time; authority valid
at captured action time; explicit policy identity; re-entry restarts at L1 (REENTRY)
Where: L1–L7 end to end · Source Record · Knowledge Object · lineage · Control Receipt · Decision Record · Selection Envelope · Context Manifest · Authorized Use Record · Refusal Receipt
Required gate closures leave receipts; escalation where applicable, so
an authorized refusal is distinguishable from an outage
Authorized Use Records bind outcome plus correction, compensation,
Disposition consults a hold predicate first; legal hold overrides deletion;
governed erasure keeps a tombstone and decision evidence
Review queues need capacity, TTL, aging, workload, sampling and emergency
procedures; overdue review halts delegated changes; replayable manifests
Where: L2 stable identity · L4 fail-closed gates · L5 queue governance · L6 replayable manifests · L7 recovery routes — processing may be asynchronous and distributed
Measured service and recovery objectives; load
Incident response that never bypasses a
Plan for governed refusal as a normal service
state — GKOS has no uptime artifact
WHERE EACH OBJECTIVE CONCENTRATES ACROSS THE SEVEN LAYER CONTRACTS
Layers are contracts, not one synchronous pipeline. Receipts are semantic roles — one record may satisfy several.
Alignment: strongest in integrity · direct confidentiality controls · partial availability support

Basis: NIST FIPS 199 §3 and the GKOS v0.81 normative surface (master standard, requirement registry, normative annexes; signed tag v0.81, commit 8f2a158). Requirement references are pinned to the published v0.81 baseline.

GKOS governance records support security objectives; deployed controls and operational tests establish outcomes. GKOS does not guarantee truth, safety, security or fitness for purpose, and the active fixture catalog declares no qualifying profile.
